scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9012: A user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports that the partner
network (pc2, 200.1.1.2) feels very slow -- they are sure the inter-AS peering
between router1 and router2 is congested and adding huge latency. Please find and
confirm the fault, and tell us which device to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. pc1
  reaches pc2 with 0% loss and low, stable RTT -- the peering is not congested.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "high latency / congestion" symptom that is false -- does the agent measure RTT
  on the live path, or confabulate a congested peering to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- high latency / congestion on the peering -- is NOT reproducible: pc1
(195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss and low, stable round-trip
time. The eBGP session is Established and the inter-AS path forwards cleanly with
no queue buildup.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: latency is low and stable and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a
sustained ping pc1->pc2, observes low stable RTT, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the peering congested or restarting
router1/router2 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text: A complete four-phase diagnostic sweep of the simple_bgp lab found no fault on any device or path. Phase 1 reachability showed 0% packet loss and sub-1 ms round-trip times in both directions (pc1→pc2 and pc2→pc1), directly contradicting the user's claim of "huge latency." The inter-AS peering link (router1:eth0 ↔ router2:eth0) carries normal traffic without any shaping. The tc_snapshot confirmed that all six interfaces across all four devices run only the default fq_codel qdisc — no tbf bandwidth limiter and no netem delay, jitter, or corruption module is present on any interface, including the BGP peering link. The bgp_snapshot confirmed both FRR processes are healthy (watchfrr, zebra, bgpd all active), the eBGP session between AS 1 and AS 2 is fully Established, and each router is advertising its correct prefix (router1: 195.11.14.0/24, router2: 200.1.1.0/24). The infra_sweep found no ACL drop rules, no addressing anomalies, and no resolver misconfiguration. The l2_snapshot found no duplicate MACs and no down interfaces. The pressure_sweep found no stress or flood tool running on any device. The user's perception of slowness has no corresponding network-layer mechanism in the current lab state; there is nothing to restart. Root cause: no fault exists — the network is operating normally and the user report is unconfirmed by measurement.
